model.drift: zero by construction, not by sample average
model.increments: iid draws from the demeaned empirical return distribution

conventions.independence: Every p-value is computed on the non-overlapping subsample. Means and histograms use every forecast.
conventions.lookahead: none: each fit sees prices up to and including its as-of date

drift_displacement.intercept_note: The intercept is pinned at 0.5 rather than fitted: a sample with no displacement must give a mean PIT of one half at every horizon, so a free intercept would absorb the effect under test.
drift_displacement.reading: A high r-squared means the location error scales as the square root of the horizon, which is what a constant per-session drift against a fixed forecast centre looks like. It is a diagnosis, not a correction: fitting a mean to remove it would be a directional forecast.

christoffersen_independence.power_note: 580 independent observations at a 1% quantile expect 5.8 breaches. The test cannot resolve a miscalibration of ordinary size at this count; read it as an absence of evidence, not as evidence of calibration.

crps.reading: Positive skill means the model beat a driftless random walk with empirical increments. Zero means it tied. Negative means it lost, and a negative number here is published rather than withheld.

direction.note: Measured against spot rather than against the forecast centre, so this gap reads the whole sample drift where the PIT mean reads only what the forecast centre failed to carry.

events.definition: terminal price above anchor x 1
events.reading: Reliability is the calibration term and lower is better; resolution is how far the forecasts move from the base rate and higher is better. A model can be perfectly reliable and useless. The decomposition is binned, so it reconstructs the exact Brier score only up to the binning error reported beside it.

events.caveat: Monitored at session close on both sides. A level breached and recovered inside one session counts for neither the forecast nor the outcome, so this probability is a floor.
